newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks seen firm if electronics renew rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks seen firm if electronics renew rise.

text.p: Taiwan share prices were expected to firm on Monday as electronics, which suffered profit-taking on Saturday, were likely to rise to fuel the upward momentum, brokers said.

Brokers said electronics, especially semiconductor shares, should rise after chip giant Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co said on Monday it would raise its 1997 sales and profit targets by more than 20 percent within 10 days due to improving performance.
On Saturday, the index surged as high as 9,021.87 but closed lower by 0.54 percent or 48.30 points at 8,833.83.
A 8,800-8,900 range was seen for Monday.
"Taiwan Semiconductor's decision to raise its profit and sales targets should boost buying in semiconductor shares," said Nomura Securities research chief Ben Lee.
"The overall index is still in a firming trend, likely to test 9,000 again in coming sessions," Lee said.
Recent bellwether financials were seen continuing their strong performance, he said.
